L01 | Judgment remains in deciding which values are long, consequential, or error-prone enough to require a copying program rather than manual transcription.
L02 | Judgment remains in deciding which possible locations or readings to check before declaring something lost and when the evidence is sufficient to act.
L03 | Judgment remains in interpreting what the person is actually asking for and resisting the urge to add technical content they did not request.
L04 | Judgment remains in deciding what actual downstream result or record count to inspect before accepting a success, ok, or clean exit.
L05 | Judgment remains in deciding how close a paraphrase is to the original and how much evidence establishes a real cause before naming one.
L06 | Judgment remains in recognizing when an empty or short result means the search failed or was truncated rather than the thing is absent.
L07 | Judgment remains in knowing when a time is important enough to read the clock rather than guess and which clock source is reliable.
L08 | Judgment remains in choosing how to force a meaningful failure and whether the test or monitor actually catches the condition it is meant to detect.
L09 | Judgment remains in deciding whether an outside source is authoritative and relevant enough to count as verification and when to say not checked.
L10 | Judgment remains in identifying which adjacent fields, components, or assumptions are likely to be affected by the fix.
L11 | Judgment remains in determining when a fact from notes, a summary, or a rulebook must be traced back and tested against its original source before being repeated.
L12 | Judgment remains in deciding which lessons are important enough to turn into built-in steps and how to design those steps so they prevent the mistake rather than just document it.
L13 | Judgment remains in deciding what kind of reviewer is different enough to catch the likely error for the work at hand.
L14 | Judgment remains in fairly assessing and stating how much and what kind of evidence a claim rests on.
L15 | Judgment remains in identifying which single check is decisive enough that work should not be called done or verified until it passes.
L16 | Judgment remains in deciding when another source or search location is likely enough to change the answer that the extra search is owed.
L17 | Judgment remains in deciding what observable behavior or output proves that a saved change or setting is actually in effect.
